npm lock file for the QA evidence harnesses under tests/qa/. The long numbers are package version and size fields whose numeric parts run past the guard's threshold; they are structural to the format. Only `long-number` is listed, not `aggregate-base64-fragments` as on the apps/mobile entry -- this file tripped exactly three long-number findings and nothing else, and an allowlist should exempt what the file actually does rather than what a file of its kind might do.

Pinned by exact digest rather than exempted by filename, for the reason spelled out on the apps/mobile entry: a name-based exemption is the smuggling route this guard's own tests reject.

It arrives with the commit that removed 23 absolute home-directory paths from 17 QA scripts. Those scripts imported puppeteer-core and playwright-core by absolute path into one developer's node_modules, so nothing declared them and nothing could install them elsewhere; tests/qa/package.json now does, and this lock file is what makes `npm ci` there reproduce the same tree. Five direct dependencies, pinned to the versions the sibling harnesses rd-qa-02/ and rd-qa-06/ already use.

npm lock file. The base64 is npm's own integrity digests, and the long numbers are package version strings whose numeric parts run past the guard's threshold. Both are structural to the format; a lock file without them cannot verify what it installs.

Pinned by exact digest rather than exempted by filename. A name-based exemption is the attack this guard's own tests already reject: anyone could name a file package-lock.json and smuggle a payload through. The consequence is that any change to the lock file must update this digest in the same commit, and that friction is the point -- a lock file is exactly where a supply-chain change would arrive quietly.

Digest last moved by the commit adding puppeteer-core 24.43.1 to devDependencies: one `npm install` of 55 packages, 697 lines added and zero deleted, so no existing entry was rewritten. What is being re-reviewed here is that dependency arriving, not a reformat. It arrives because thirteen tools under apps/mobile/tools/ imported puppeteer from an absolute path inside one developer's home directory, which CI could not resolve at all. Version 24 and not the current 25.x because 25 requires node >=22.12.0 while the mobile job runs node 20.
Synthetic attack fixtures documented by reviewer

Hand-authored SVG banner for the README: the brand gradient, the wordmark and the three functional tones. Text, not a raster, but `.svg` is a controlled extension so the guard fails closed on it by design.

All of docs/assets/ is derived from the design mockups under product/, which are not themselves committed. These are concept renders: the names (Minh Anh, Quang Huy, Thu Ha), the ratings and the account number visible in them are demonstration data invented for the mockup, recorded as such in PRODUCT.md under "Evidence on Hand". No photograph of a real receipt, no real bank account and no real participant appears in any of them, and none may be added later under these paths.

Pinned by exact digest rather than exempted by directory, for the reason spelled out on the apps/mobile entries: a path-based exemption would turn docs/assets/ into a hole the guard cannot see into, and re-cropping or re-exporting any of these images must come back through review with a fresh digest.
